knowledge:
- key_parameters: gact=Genotype matrix where rows are markers and columns are individuals ;; gexp=Gene expression matrix where rows are genes and columns are individuals ;; gpos=Data frame containing marker physical positions (chromosome, physical position) ;; ppos=Data frame containing gene physical positions (chromosome, start, end) ;; window=Genomic distance in base pairs to define local (cis) linkage ;; prob.cutoff=Posterior probability threshold for establishing a causal link in the network
- alternatives: qtl for standard QTL mapping, WGCNA for undirected co-expression network analysis, and pcalg for general causal graph estimation without genetic anchors
- when_to_use: When matched genotype and high-dimensional gene expression data are available for a segregating population (e.g., yeast crosses, recombinant inbred lines) and the goal is to infer directed causal regulatory networks
- pitfalls: Requires exact matching of sample IDs across genotype and expression datasets; assumes a simple causal model (genotype -> regulator -> target) which may miss complex feedback loops; computationally intensive for large datasets, requiring pre-filtering of genes and markers

workflows.name: causal_network_inference
workflows.intent: Reconstruct causal transcriptional regulatory networks from matched genotype and gene expression data using eQTL-directed graphical models.
input: genotypes.txt (matrix of marker genotypes across individuals)
expression.txt (matrix of gene expression levels across individuals)
workflows.stages: 1. Build the trigger object using trigger.build ;; 2. Compute local linkage (eQTLs) using trigger.loclink ;; 3. Estimate the posterior probabilities of causal regulation using trigger.prob ;; 4. Reconstruct the causal network using trigger.net ;; 5. Export the network using trigger.export
workflows.code:
trig <- trigger.build(gact = gact, gexp = gexp, gpos = gpos, ppos = ppos)
trig.loc <- trigger.loclink(trig, window = 100000)
trig.prob <- trigger.prob(trig.loc, logratio = TRUE)
trig.net <- trigger.net(trig.prob, prob.cutoff = 0.9)
trigger.export(trig.net, file = "causal_network.txt")
